newsitem.title: NORWAY: OSLO BOURSE PEAKS ON COMPANY PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: OSLO BOURSE PEAKS ON COMPANY PROFITS.

text.p: Norwegian shares stormed to the third consecutive all-time high on Thursday after several companies reported healthy first-half 1997 profits, dealers said.
Oslo's Total share index rallied to a record close of 1,332.17 points, up 1.23 percent. Turnover was heavy at 1.58 billion crowns.
Shares in drugs company Nycomed rose sharply on following the release of better-than-expected first-half 1997 profits. Nycomed's A share jumped 4.33 percent to 168.50 crowns.
"The result was better than expected in several divisions," an Oslo dealer said. "Things look good in the United States."
Nycomed plans to merge with Britain's Amersham International Plc soon.
"This was a positive result and it increases the chances for the merger to come through," the dealer said.
Shares in offshore supply company Aker Maritime ASA jumped 14.3 percent to 136 crowns after the group presented better than expected results.
Shares in airliner Braathens SAFE, which also presented healty profits, closed 19.4 percent up at 86 crowns.
